Standard: The AR system design and installation allow spatial separation between vehicles to avoid collision and negative impacts to engine performance, flight control and stability, or structure or components of either air vehicle. a. Boom/Receptacle air vehicle. Boom/Receptacle system design and location allow receptacle receiver to maintain attitude, velocity, and position throughout the extents of the boom envelope without degradation to air vehicle or engine performance or collision with tanker or other receiver air vehicle. For simultaneous receivers, the separation distance between receivers is at least 0.25 wingspan of the largest winged receiver that will be simultaneously refueled. b. Probe/Drogue air vehicle. Probe/drogue system installation allows probe receiver to make contact and refuel throughout the fuel transfer zone without degradation to air vehicle performance or collision with the tanker or other receiver air vehicle. The nose of the receiver is aft of the tail of the tanker when engaged in refueling position at least 15 ft forward of full trail. For simultaneous receivers, the separation distance between receivers is at least 0.25 wingspan of the largest winged receiver that will be simultaneously refueled. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker/Receptacle Receiver. Examination of air vehicle drawings and models verifies separation exists between tanker and receiver at receiver positions: precontact, contact, and the corners of the boom disconnect envelope. Required separation exists between receivers when simultaneously refueling multiple air vehicles (if applicable). b. Drogue Tanker/Probe Receiver. Examination of air vehicle drawings and models verifies separation exists between tanker and receiver at receiver positions: precontact, contact, and inner and outer hose refueling limits. Separation exists between receivers when simultaneously refueling multiple air vehicles (if applicable). Analysis.
  (1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker/Receptacle Receiver. Aerodynamic modeling verifies tanker engine exhaust does not impinge on receiver structure and tanker wake does not negatively impact receiver engine performance, flight controls, stability or structure at receiver positions: precontact, contact, and the corners of the boom disconnect envelope. b. Drogue Tanker/Probe Receiver. Aerodynamic modeling verifies tanker engine exhaust does not impinge on receiver structure and tanker wake and downwash effects do not negatively impact receiver engine performance, flight controls, stability or structure at receiver positions: precontact, contact, and within the hose refueling range. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (1) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker/Receptacle Receiver. Evaluations of air vehicle performance during AR flight test show no negative impacts to air vehicle response, stability and control, engine performance, ram air cooling, and air data system performance. b. Drogue Tanker/Probe Receiver. Evaluations of air vehicle performance during AR flight test show no negative impacts to air vehicle response, stability and control, engine performance, ram air cooling, and air data system performance.
